content.content:
Applied by a reviewer reading the recorded nodes; nothing runs. Read the dependent's recorded decision against each recorded prerequisite in turn.

(1) Licence against mwwxxzyk — no element of the dependent contradicts mwwxxzyk: fail, naming the element and the prerequisite it contradicts, if any element of the dependent forbids, reverses or substitutes an outcome that prerequisite fixes, or narrows the prerequisite by excepting a case the prerequisite covers.

(2) Licence against wtywxppt — no element of the dependent contradicts any value wtywxppt records under its element, aspect, state, value or note keys: fail, naming the element and the prerequisite it contradicts, if any element of the dependent forbids, reverses or substitutes a recorded value, or narrows the prerequisite by excepting a case the prerequisite covers.

(3) The check presumes no element of the dependent and no particular prerequisite clause; which element is at issue is a finding named only in the check's output. It requires no wording, sentence order or vocabulary of the dependent, and invents no rule the prerequisites do not state.

(4) A placeholder, empty or ref-less commitment in the dependent, or in a prerequisite the check is read against, leaves the check with no recorded subject: fail, naming the placeholder.
content.rationale:
rqrlnzny uses mwwxxzyk for the link presentation its pointer cue presumes — the pointer is the cue that an entry is activatable, so this decision must not re-decide which listed entries are links — and wtywxppt for the pointer-precision commitment it spends on the entry, which it must not spend as a claim on the other axis that prerequisite's note records.

mwwxxzyk is a commitment in words (content type text, inline) and so sits on the natural layer; rqrlnzny is likewise a commitment in words, so the mwwxxzyk use is the eval-matrix's natural-to-natural cell — evals/natural-to-natural.md, whose licence check is copied as clause (1). wtywxppt is a visual-spec: an inline JSON object with a fixed key grammar (element, aspect, state, value, note), so it sits on the structured layer, and the child stays natural; the matrix has no structured-to-natural cell, so that use takes the documented default — the same gate form — and is flagged here for a matrix entry, the same gap lvqyqozt flagged for its structured-to-natural edge and wurvunqu took as the floor for a visual-spec prerequisite. One criterion carries both uses because both ask the same question of the same dependent text — does it contradict a prerequisite it was drawn against — and because a second evaluation would gate two layer pairs that resolve to one form.

Neither clause demands an observable. Both prerequisites, and the child, are commitments in words: the dependent decides an appearance cue rather than behaviour, so demanding a rendered cursor, a rendered entry or a hit target from this node would exceed the child's layer and pre-empt the code-layer carriers, which are gated where the stylesheet and the panel actually become artifacts — U7's and U8's amended evaluations. Clause (2)'s known scope, stated so the gate is not read as stronger than it is: wtywxppt's element field fixes canvas elements, so on a detail-panel entry the licence is the pointer-precision commitment its note and rationale carry, not its min 24px value, and the check cannot demand a hit target for an entry; nor can it catch a dependent that claimed the keyboard half of that note, because no recorded prerequisite of this node states who owns keyboard cues. Both limits keep the check at non-violation instead of inventing a rule.

Clause (4) lets the criterion be applied as soon as the dependent carries a recorded decision and makes an unauthored or ref-less subject a named failure rather than a silent pass. The criterion never defines rqrlnzny, restates it, or tracks its wording; rewording the decision without changing what it decides leaves every clause intact.
